task: Core #1186 F6-U03f: guarded transaction-local Fresh Install identity/data/dependency preflight, SQL execution disabled

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Critical risk: compile future in-transaction database identity/row/catalog/role checks as a guarded review artifact, not a live reset. Preserve immutable one-project external TLS binding, fail-closed proof semantics, known App/managed boundaries, and exact-head CI.

acceptanceCriteria: Canonical source review emits a BEGIN/SET LOCAL/guard/abort-before-DROP/59-file candidate with no hosted SQL execution path.
Transaction guard locks every nonpartition app relation NOWAIT before mutable row inventory and refuses unknown user/business rows, catalogs, SQL object drift and managed dependencies.
One local PostgreSQL service job exercises the transaction-guard primitive for success, unexpected row, neutral hash mismatch, NOWAIT lock and role/target mismatch without accessing Supabase.
Exact grant/event/known Auth trigger snapshots are checked without weakening previously discovered ACL safety requirements.
Exact-head canonical Quality Tests, TypeScript, build, Completion Truth and Lifecycle must PASS; hosted Fresh Install remains BLOCKED.
invariants: Guard statement must appear inside BEGIN and before all DROP statements and before permanent abort-before-DROP barrier.
Unsafe or missing target bindings never grant authority to invoke hosted destructive SQL.
All seven neutral catalog table hashes are compared to immutable pinned historical fingerprints; any extra row on any other app table aborts.
Known Auth dependency and six event trigger function identities, public/private ACLs and Storage boundaries remain required checks.
These changes do not become a parallel Control Plane or independent release READY authority.
forbiddenStates: An executable hosted schema-reset mode is added to code or workflow.
Database identity inferred only from current_database='postgres' is treated as proof of specific Supabase project.
Lock timeout or unexpected table/dependency rows are silently tolerated.
An invariant-mismatched snapshot produces claim of accepted migration readiness.
A passing fixture is labeled as Fresh Install 59 migrations or signed-in Alap/Pro permission proof.

failureModes: NOWAIT table locks are skipped, a customer row appears after count checks and is deleted.
App row checks verify only known neutral tables, leaving a hidden user row unexamined.
Neutral catalog count matches but changed cell values are ignored.
External Auth trigger is dropped by CASCADE and missing after source assembly.
Schema ACLs are not restored despite migration success.
The platform project has the same current_database, role and version as Fresh Install and could be mistakenly targeted.
Managed Storage file transfer appears between preflight and COMMIT.
An unconditional review-only abort is moved after DROP by a refactor.
edgeCases: Unknown app relation under public/private, partitioned tables and sequences.
One new row in a previously empty customer or Office table.
Single neutral entitlement row changed but count unchanged.
Known Auth trigger changed function identity or a new managed dependent view.
One extra bucket, changed limit, changed provider event trigger function digest.
NOWAIT lock conflict from a concurrent session and forced statement timeout.
Restored grants to anon/authenticated missing, or anon receives CREATE.
Disconnected client near COMMIT must be classified UNKNOWN until independent postflight.

alternatives.summary: Add transaction-local SQL safety gate only to non-executable reviewed 59-file candidate.
alternatives.reason: Ensures realistic future DDL guard ordering with zero hosted migration risk.

alternatives.summary: Execute new guard then DROP public/private on current Fresh Install database.
alternatives.reason: One read-only snapshot is not a transactional live authorization, and full provider quiescence / exact TLS binding remains unproven.

alternatives.summary: Keep using prior standalone snapshot alone and declare reset ready.
alternatives.reason: Does not lock or revalidate mutable state inside one transaction.

specialistReviews.finding: postgres/17/database=postgres is shared across Supabase projects.
specialistReviews.resolution: Explicitly mark project identity as outside-DB TLS verification unproved; never use SQL checks alone to authorize target DDL.

specialistReviews.finding: Historical snapshot is stale without locks and immutable hash comparison.
specialistReviews.resolution: Add NOWAIT locks, full app-row inventory and neutral JSONB hashes in transaction; fail closed.

specialistReviews.finding: F6-U03b candidate must remain intentionally aborting before any schema DROP.
specialistReviews.resolution: Enforce source ordering and execution-disabled contract in unit tests and canonical CI.

specialistReviews.finding: Passing source-only SQL generation may be mistakenly promoted to hosted Fresh Install READY.
specialistReviews.resolution: Only claim review compiler improvement; preserve existing Completion Truth scope and separate future hosted proof.

challenge.scenario: Correct database/role but wrong Supabase project.
challenge.finding: SQL-only identity is not unique across projects.
challenge.resolution: Treat exact project ref + TLS peer checks as an external mandatory future dependency; review artifact is never executable hosted.

challenge.scenario: Customer/Office rows appear between snapshot and DROP.
challenge.finding: Historical zero counts do not protect subsequent user writes.
challenge.resolution: Acquire bounded NOWAIT ACCESS EXCLUSIVE application locks then inventory every application row in the same transaction.

challenge.scenario: Neutral table count matches but user changes entitlement data.
challenge.finding: Counts are insufficient for catalog integrity.
challenge.resolution: Require seven exact deterministic JSONB MD5 row-content fingerprints.

challenge.scenario: Application function or RLS policy changed while table counts remain 177.
challenge.finding: Row tables do not measure schema semantic identity.
challenge.resolution: Require exact historical object-definition catalog hash before future DDL.

challenge.scenario: Extra managed trigger depends on private schema.
challenge.finding: Dropping private CASCADE can destroy new provider hooks.
challenge.resolution: Recheck normalized pg_depend and require one exact known Auth dependency, unknown classes fail.

challenge.scenario: A correctly replayed 59-file application schema is exposed to authenticated/anon traffic after DROP/CREATE without restoring their old namespace USAGE grants.
challenge.finding: Although the new tables, policies and functions may exist, PostgreSQL CREATE SCHEMA resets the old named-role USAGE and CREATE privileges, causing unavailable Data API paths and potentially incorrect access.
challenge.resolution: Before hosted authorization, require an exact regrant of the five documented public and three private role ACLs in the same transaction, with negative checks that anon/authenticated cannot CREATE and independent postflight Data API proof.

challenge.scenario: Managed Storage data changes while app tables are locked.
challenge.finding: Application locks do not freeze managed schemas and traffic.
challenge.resolution: No hosted reset in this unit; future authorization requires quiescence and managed-state recheck with provider-level coordination.

challenge.scenario: The code is invoked as SQL and executes DROP on expected schema without PO signoff.
challenge.finding: A syntactically executable guarded transaction is still destructive.
challenge.resolution: Retain permanent intentional RAISE EXCEPTION before DROP; no hosted-runner path and no secret in CI.

proofPlan: Canonical Development Guard Plan Before Code validates exact projected files, owners, negative knowledge and critical-risk depth.
Source-level guarded SQL tests check transaction lock order, fail-stop drift predicates and hard abort-before-DROP.
Real ephemeral PG fixture verifies lock conflict and abnormal app data abort on same transaction, without hosted secrets.
Separate read-only Fresh Install endpoint confirms pinned 175/2 app tables and seven neutral row-content digests but is not deletion authority.
Canonical exact-head Quality Tests, TypeScript, Production Build, Completion Truth and Lifecycle closure.
No hosted provider SQL mutation, 59-file migration execution or Office Alap/Pro RLS proof.
operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Fresh Install current historical schema cannot be reset until the future SQL transaction can recheck exact destination identity, lock all app tables and validate all application row inventories, seven neutral catalogs, 4621 canonical catalog definitions, external auth trigger, bucket/role/event definitions and zero managed Auth/Storage/migration state. The source-pinned 59-file review transaction is deliberately executable only up to a permanent pre-DROP RAISE EXCEPTION; the new guard must remain review-only.
observableOutcomes: An immutable SQL fragment performs transaction-scoped DB/role/version/PG application_name checks, uses pg_try_advisory_xact_lock plus NOWAIT bounded app-table locks before scanning rows.

Inside the same transaction, the code enumerates every existing public/private table, rejects any non-neutral rows, compares seven exact neutral row counts/hashes and refuses mismatched object inventory.
The guard validates the known external auth.users trigger, namespace owners/ACLs and managed Auth/Storage/event boundaries; unknown evidence blocks.
Integration of the SQL fragment into existing 59-file review compiler occurs while retaining the unconditional abort-before-DROP invariant and with zero database transports.
A separate fixture-only PostgreSQL17 workflow may exercise lock/rollback primitives without touching any Supabase project; the actual hosted 59-file reset/tenant proof stays blocked.
unresolvedRisks: SQL current_database/postgres role/version cannot distinguish the platform from Fresh Install; outside-DB TLS/project endpoint binding is a mandatory independent condition.

The protected managed Auth/Storage user state cannot be exhaustively frozen by application-table locks; future hosted authorization must include provider traffic quiescence and a separately approved target-only execution path.
Provider event-trigger effects and PostgREST data API readiness are not covered by the source-only SQL fragment.
Textual SQL review cannot establish proof of actual hosted rollback/migration/Alap-Pro RLS; executable proof requires separate governed permission.

in: Introduce immutable, source-reviewed PostgreSQL SQL preflight generator with transaction-local app locks and strict row/catalog/dependency/ACL/managed-state checks.
Wire the preflight BEFORE the existing hard abort barrier and before any destructive SQL in the F6-U03b 59-file candidate without enabling hosted execution.
Add adversarial unit tests for target/role mismatch, neutral table hash drift, unknown data, event/ACL drift and SQL statement ordering.
Use existing canonical Development Guard, Plan Before Code, CI, Completion Truth, Lifecycle; document explicit no-hosted-action boundary.
out: No actual SQL execution on any hosted Supabase project, no DDL and no migration application.
No loosening existing F6-U03b fail-before-DROP or F6-U03e fixture-only transport policies.
No extra active Supabase project, no platform/staging status changes.
No claim of actual 59-file hosted replay, provider event readiness, Data API exposure or signed-in Alap/Pro RLS proof.

requirements.requirement: Before any destructive SQL, re-check database role/version and exact owned app rows with NOWAIT transactional locks and immutable catalog fingerprints.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Unknown user row or neutral catalog hash drift passes the reviewed SQL guard.

requirements.requirement: Require known managed Auth/Storage/ACL/DDL-event dependencies and fail closed on any unknown exception.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Unknown provider dependence or lost schema role privileges is ignored.

requirements.requirement: Keep compiled 59-file future transaction deliberately non-executable before DROP and prohibit any cloud runner or reset-ready overclaim.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A CLI or GitHub workflow enables the hosted 59-file destructive replay.
